symptoms: Status Epilepticus (SE): Seizure > 5 min OR >2 seizures without recovery to baseline.
Refractory SE: Ongoing seizure activity despite adequately dosed 1st and 2nd line agents.
Super-refractory SE: Ongoing seizure activity for >24 hrs, OR despite 2 AEDs or 3rd line anaesthetic agents.

management_steps.details: Left lateral position, non-rebreather facemask, simple airway manoeuvres, prep BMV + OPA, prep intubation. DEFG: 1ml/kg 50% Dextrose + 100mg Thiamine IM. Check Sodium: if < 115 mmol/L, give 100mL 3% Saline.
If No IV: Midazolam 0,2mg/kg IMI (max 10mg IM). If IV in situ: Lorazepam 0,1mg/kg (max 8mg over 2 minutes) OR Clonazepam 0,02mg/kg (max 2mg over 30 sec). Repeat benzo dose x1 after 5 minutes.
Sodium Valproate 20mg/kg IV at 5mg/kg/min (~5min) OR Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV at 50mg/min (~25min). Repeat AED at 1/2 dose after 20 minutes if still seizing.

Propofol Infusion 1-4mg/kg/hr (add adrenaline for vasodilation/hypotension). Midazolam Infusion 0,1mg/kg/hr. Ketofol Infusion. Phenobarbital 20mg/kg per NG (crush tablets with sterile water). Pyridoxine 5g per NGT (for INH induced seizures).

warnings: Omit 2nd line agents for toxin-induced seizures.
Do not unnecessarily delay airway management for AEDs to take effect.
Phenobarbital may be considered 1st/2nd line in neonates / small infants.
